CO-7.name: Brittany Pettersen
CO-7.evidence: Incumbent; New Democrat Coalition member and Future Forum co-chair in a Solid D seat (plain New Dem in safe seat -> liberal); conventional party-backed profile. Wayback blocked; no dated page fetched.

NC-9.name: Richard Ojeda
NC-9.evidence: Campaign: 'fight for working people - not Donald Trump', cost-of-living focus, small-donor base; endorsed by NC Dem Party Progressive Caucus, NEA, American People's Compact (no JD/DSA/Sanders markers -> liberal). Long-running populist working-class brand.

MA-9.name: Bill Keating
MA-9.evidence: Nine-term incumbent running on experience; labor-funded; original Medicare for All Act cosponsor but defends ACA; primary challenger called him a 'corporate establishment Democrat'.

MN-5.name: Ilhan Omar
MN-5.evidence: Co-chair of the Medicare for All Caucus; Squad member (memory); campaign emphasises 'co-governance'; now a DFL-endorsed incumbent seeking fifth term (left insurgent turned incumbent -> mixed).

SEN-GA.name: Jon Ossoff
SEN-GA.evidence: Incumbent re-running anti-corruption message; campaign casts him as 'watchdog who has challenged powerful institutions', ads on Collins siding with 'powerful elites'; bipartisan foster-care investigation; heavy institutional fundraising.

TN-7.name: Darden Copeland
TN-7.evidence: Self-described: 'I'm simply a moderate', 'I'm simply not a socialist' (reportedly also 'Blue Dog' Democrat); pitches as outsider not a career politician, but is CEO of a Nashville public-affairs firm and self-funded vs Behn.

GOV-NH.name: Cinde Warmington
GOV-NH.evidence: Executive Councilor, former health-care lobbyist; affordability message ('prices ... crushing working families') and standing up to Trump; conventional party framing, unopposed for nomination.

TX-31.name: Justin Early
TX-31.evidence: Backs Green New Deal, universal publicly funded health care, federal jobs guarantee, court expansion, but no left-org endorsements found; party insider background (precinct chair, 2008 Obama delegate); Dell cybersecurity architect, Army veteran.

OH-13.name: Emilia Sykes
OH-13.evidence: Frontline incumbent in competitive seat; New Democrat Coalition member, DCCC touts her as 'one of the most bipartisan Democrats in Ohio'; former Ohio House Minority Leader. No dated page successfully fetched (Daily Signal 403).

VA-11.name: James Walkinshaw
VA-11.evidence: Connolly's chief of staff for 10 years and Fairfax supervisor; mainstream Democratic platform (abortion rights, federal workers, housing, economy for 'everyone, not just billionaires'); successor-incumbent.

VA-6.name: Beth Macy
VA-6.evidence: 'Just for working people, not necessarily Dems or Republicans', working-class background, no corporate PAC money, 'I can't be bought, and I can't be controlled', unsure establishment likes her; supports Medicare for All but no Sanders/OR/WFP backing found.

MI-9.name: Ray Pooley
MI-9.evidence: First-time candidate, CNC machinist / 'third-generation manufacturer'; Medicare for All, CEO-to-worker pay ratio cap, break corporate health monopolies, tax ultra-wealthy; no endorsements, minimal funds.

SEN-WV.name: Rachel Fetty Anderson
SEN-WV.evidence: Public-interest attorney, ex-Morgantown council; campaign 'rejects foreign and corporate money', will reverse 'laws that reward donors', 'root out politicians who rob taxpayers'; beat the self-styled most-progressive candidate in primary.
